messages.content: Choose exactly one frozen method for this research benchmark partition BEFORE seeing any association labels, held-out metrics or other partition outcomes. Call submit_partition_choice once. Use only the supplied expression-feature summary and method definitions. If the summary is insufficient, still choose one method and state the uncertainty. Do not claim efficacy or unseen performance.

{"dataset": "TRANSCRIPT v2.0.0 disease partition", "disease_count": 33, "drug_count": 613, "expression_gene_count": 12096, "median_disease_signature_sd": 0.00847, "methods": {"B0p": "Training-fold positive association count per drug", "B1": "Label-free negative Spearman correlation between drug and disease expression", "B1k": "Training-fold label propagation from expression-similar drugs with 10 neighbors", "B2": "Fixed equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion of B0p, B1k and B1 with k=60"}, "metric_to_optimize": "official NS-AUC", "partition_id": "transcript_disease_partition_03", "split": "random_simple", "split_description": "Hold out 20% of drug-disease pairs; the same drugs may occur in training"}

function.name: submit_partition_choice
function.arguments: {"method": "B0p", "reason": "This is a random_simple pair-level split, not a drug-cold-start split, so training-fold positive counts per drug (B0p) can exploit the fact that the same drugs reappear in training. With 33 diseases and 613 drugs, per-drug association counts provide a direct, stable ranking signal learned from training folds, and B0p alone is the single method that most directly uses the observed label structure that survives this split. The expression-based methods (B1, B1k) depend on a disease signature with a very small median SD (0.00847), suggesting weak/noisy expression signal, and B2 only fuses components whose individual value is uncertain here. B0p also avoids the risk that the label-free correlation (B1) carries little ranking information for official NS-AUC. This choice is made on the provided summary alone; no performance claims are implied."}
